title: What's your Mars sign about?
old_caption:
Mars takes about 687 days to circle the Sun. In astrology it stands for drive: how you go after things and how you face conflict.
It isn't your angry sign. Think of it as fuel, not a fuse.

title: Why does Mercury run your texts?
old_caption: In astrology, Mercury rules how we think and talk, which makes it the planet of your messages. The playful takeaway is solid advice: think first, then text.

title: Cardinal, fixed, mutable: what?
old_caption:
Cardinal signs start, fixed signs hold, mutable signs adapt. Each season begins as the Sun enters a cardinal sign.
Like a relay: start it, hold it, pass it on. Every mode has a role to play.

title: Why does my Moon sign matter?
old_caption:
The Moon crosses a whole sign in about two and a half days. In astrology it stands for your feelings and what comforts you on a hard day.
Your Moon sign is a bit like your blanket fort.

title: Is it needy to have needs?
old_caption: Having needs doesn't make you needy. Everyone has them, and saying them clearly is healthy. A need is a request, not a demand. Asking isn't weakness.

title: What are the lunar nodes?
old_caption:
The lunar nodes are where the Moon's path crosses the Sun's, and eclipses happen near them. Astrologers read the north node as growth and the south as comfort.
Grow toward your north, gently.

title: Do opposite signs attract?
old_caption: Opposite signs sit across the zodiac wheel, and astrologers read them as mirrors. Fun to explore. Just remember attraction happens between people, not birth dates.

title: How fast is too fast?
old_caption:
Met Tuesday, already booked a trip? There's no right speed for love, only a matched one.
Ask "is this pace good for you?" and notice if you feel rushed. "Slower, please" is a full sentence.

title: How do you fix a fight?
old_caption:
Winning a fight can still leave you feeling worse. Fights aren't won, they're repaired.
Start soft with "I feel," take a real break if it's heated, then reconnect with something small like "I hear you."

title: Do planets really go backwards?
old_caption:
Planets don't actually reverse. Retrograde is apparent motion, like passing a slower car on the highway. Astrologers read it as a time to review.
Re-read the text, take a breath, no need to panic.
